event.label: Biden’s surprise visit to Kyiv
event.description: Nine reports cover Biden’s February 20 Kyiv visit, its aid announcements, preparation and interpretations of its purpose. Promises, reported private talks and commentators’ forecasts are kept separate.

topics.label: Planning and warning Russia
topics.scope_note: Secret preparation and advance notification are separate from a claim that the visit was risk-free.

topics.label: The message of continued support
topics.scope_note: A president’s promise and an analyst’s interpretation of the visit’s message are different kinds of evidence.

topics.label: New military aid
topics.scope_note: An announcement or promise is not proof that equipment or money had already arrived. Repeated accounts may rely on CNN or one White House statement.

topics.label: Further penalties on Russia
topics.scope_note: Announced plans for further penalties are separate from measures already in force.

topics.label: Why did Biden visit?
topics.scope_note: Reassurance, battlefield talks and pressure for progress can coexist. Different accounts of purpose need not be factual contradictions.

topics.label: What might the visit change?
topics.scope_note: Predictions about battlefield effects or Russian reactions are not observed outcomes.

topics.label: Biden’s view of Russia’s plans
topics.scope_note: Biden’s judgments about Putin’s calculations are attributed political assessments, not independent access to Putin’s thoughts.

topics.label: Travel and meetings after Kyiv
topics.scope_note: One report may describe a planned onward trip and another its later departure; that time difference is not a contradiction.

method.country_note: Outlet countries describe origin. Claimant countries describe an office, organization or stated residence, not assumed citizenship.
method.claim_type_note: A fact claim is a checkable statement, not a fact verified by this graph. Opinions, predictions, legal positions and promises are marked separately.
method.edge_note: Green arrows point from a claim supplying a reason, example or reported statement to the specified part of another claim. Grey comparisons have no assigned evidential direction. Solid red connections mark proposed contradictions between specific claims or assessments. An arrow is used for an explicit rebuttal of a matching claim. Repeated reports of the same statement share a source.
method.attention_note: Attention is a qualitative reading of the saved article, with paragraph locators; it is not a measured share of words.
method.endorsement_note: A quoted speaker’s view is separate from the article narrator’s view. No outlet-wide position is inferred from one article.
method.cleaning_note: Uses saved recovered text. Kyiv Independent later Most Popular / News Feed material is excluded; original paragraph numbers retained. FT wrapped lines are joined into logical paragraphs. CNN and Sputnik each have one long extracted paragraph; evidence quotes isolate complete relevant sentences instead of duplicating the whole article for each claim.
